en: Sure... Of course.
Come see me again if you want to keep learning the secrets of true beauty.
A lady mustn't neglect her hair, and so I want you to visit my favorite hair salon. It's called Hair Message Lovesong, and it's over in Shofukucho. It's on the same street as your agency.
Ooh, I like your enthusiasm. Let's get right to it then, shall we?
You're making a fair amount of progress, and your beauty is coming along.
What, really? I don't think I'm⑬
What a pure and sweet reaction. Oh, bumpkin. I was only flattering you!
If you were a song, you'd be at the chorus. In other words, you still have a ways to go.
It feels a long way off to me.
Well, anyway. It sure is cold, isn't it?
I know. I'm freezing.
Cold weather can be hard on the hair, and you're living proof, bumpkin. I mean, talk about a haircare disaster!
What!? Really?
You can't fool these eyes. Are you taking proper care of your hair?
I mean... As much as the next girl.
What did I tell you about that? "As much as the next girl" simply won't do! You have to take care of your appearance if you want to live in the limelight.
Bumpkin, I want you to pay a visit to my favorite salon.
You want me to cut my hair?
No, silly! Just a treatment. My hair stylist there will turn that bird nest of yours into the loveliest of locks.
He's quite the stud muffin, so I'm sure you'll recognize him right away.
Okay, where is this salon?
Over in Shofukucho. It's called Hair Message Lovesong. It's on the same street as your agency.
Okay, I'll stop by when I have a chance.
Oh, and make sure you bring at least 20,000 yen with you.
Yoko-san, I bought some takoyaki!
Well, what're you waiting for, bumpkin? Let's have it.
Hmph... Didn't you hear what I said?
I wanted a sixteen-piece order of takoyaki from Magutako.
You got that?
Sorry... I'll try again.
Yes, this is exactly what I wanted. You're not half bad when you put your mind to it, bumpkin.
Um, you're welcome?
Well, time to chow down.
Whew, that hit the spot. Here's that book, just like I promised.
Thank you! Let's see here... Oh, right, I get it!
I take it you find it useful?
Very! I mean, this is amazing, Yoko-san! I can't believe the person who wrote this book is right in front of me!
I'm not sure if that's a compliment or not, but I'll give you the benefit of the doubt and say thank you.
Get me some takoyaki, and I'll give you this book of mine. I'm partial to Magutako's takoyaki. Sixteen pieces should do the trick.
Well, bumpkin? Did you find what you were looking for?
I checked around at all the bookstores, but it was sold out no matter where I tried.
Is that right? I guess I'm a more popular author than I thought.
(I probably shouldn't say one place had it on sale and another had a used copy.)
So, um, how am I supposed to get a copy of that book now?
Tsk, fine, you can have my copy.
Of course, it's going to cost you! Hmm, let's see...
Actually, I'm kind of hungry. I could go for some takoyaki from Magutako. Theirs is the best!
Takoyaki?
That's right. You are capable of buying some takoyaki, aren't you, bumpkin?
Okay, one order of takoyaki coming up.
Whoa, slow down.
Make sure you order the sixteen-piece takoyaki. Okay, off you go.

I want people to notice how much you take care of your appearance, but teaching you everything you need to know is a hassle. Just read the book I wrote. You should be able to find it at any of Sotenbori's bookstores.
Are those your street clothes? Well, they're rather plain, to be honest.
Really? I like this outfit...
Listen, bumpkin. Fans live out their dreams through artists like you.
That's true...
So you can never let your guard down, even offstage. You never know who might be watching.
I understand. So what should I do?
I'm not saying you have to wear brand-name outfits or anything.
But sadly, people tend to judge books by their covers.
So you need to learn how to maintain a proper appearance. Make people notice how much you care about it.
I have a best-selling book that explains everything you need to know. Go buy it at a local bookstore.
Can't you just give me a copy?
Don't be silly! I'm not one to let a sale slip by, especially to a captive market.
Plus, your appeal is guaranteed to skyrocket if you read my book. It's a small price to pay.
Now, stop grumbling about it and go buy a copy!
(I bet Yoko-san's book is packed with useful information.)
(I think there was a big bookstore on Sotenbori St. East, right across from Kani Douraku. Maybe I'll try looking there.)
Looks like your salon visit went well.
Yes, Momiyama-san is really something else.
Isn't he just? He's so good with his hands, it's like he's got eight of them!
I'm joking, bumpkin! Don't you have a witty comeback or something?
Er, are we talking about a man or an octopus?
Oh my, you really are a bumpkin, aren't you? Anyway, how do you feel?
I feel great! I didn't realize how amazing a salon could be.
Is that it? You didn't notice anything during your battle with Momi-chan?
You mean the dance battle? Hmm, let me think...
His dancing skills are rather lacking, and that's putting it kindly.
But he was just so determined! I couldn't take my eyes off of him.
Exactly. You don't have to be the best at what you do, but if you put everything you've got into it, people will find you quite appealing.
It's confidence and passion that people find appealing, wouldn't you agree?
Yes, I think you're right!
You can use <Color:7>Idol Heat<Color:Default> in concert battles more often now.
See Upgrades in the pause menu for more information.
Wait, have you been trying to teach me that all along?
Maybe I was, maybe I wasn't. But I don't know much about dancing. I've dedicated my life to seeking true beauty.

I want you to beat the manager of the salon I go to in a dance battle. I asked him to give you a free session if you win. You'll find him over at a building south of Bishamon Bridge. He should be out in front of his shop looking for opponents.
You're an idol, right, bumpkin?
Yes, I am.
Then might I recommend you go on a diet?
You know what I'm talking about.
I know how hungry you can get at your age.
Hehe, it's true.
But that's no excuse for poor eating habits!
Right! Sorry!
Well, I know just what to do. I'll have you pay a visit to the beauty salon that I frequent.
A beauty salon?
Yes, it's great. In fact, it's a must for anyone who wants to maintain a girlish figure. And it's great for anti-aging treatments, too!
I've never been to a salon before. It sounds expensive.
Don't be silly. It only costs around 80,000 yen.
Oh, shame. Perhaps that seems a bit pricey to a bumpkin like you.
Well, more than a bit, actually.
I'll tell you what. The manager there is an acquaintance of mine.
And it just happens that he's hooked on dance battles.
Really? Dance battles?
I know. He should start acting his age. But in any case, aren't you into dance battles, too?
I am, but I don't have much experience yet.
Well, you go beat him in a dance battle. I'll ask him to give you a free treatment session if you win.
Are sure it's all right?
Why wouldn't it be? I mean, he and I are really close. Would you like to know how close?
Um... No, that's okay. I'll pass.
So where should I go to meet him? Please tell me, Yoko-san!
Now slow down, bumpkin. You got a lot more enthusiastic once you heard it was free.
He's always out in front of his shop looking for opponents. It's south of Bishamon Bridge.
Yoko-san, I picked up the Chinese medicine you told me about.
Wonderful, bumpkin. Make sure you use it on your skin every morning and every night.
Oh, okay. But why this instead of a more modern cosmetic?
It's natural and relatively easy on the body. I don't trust some of the chemicals they want us to slather all over ourselves.
Chinese medicine is wonderful in any case. You can get prescriptions tailor-made for your own specific condition, you see.
And all Chinese medicine helps a lady stay beautiful.
Oh, I had no idea Chinese medicine could do all that.
Whoever figured all this out must've had ideas similar to my secrets of true beauty.
Well, the mind and body are connected, but when they get out of whack, Chinese medicine helps restore the balance between them.
The secrets of true beauty are basically the same way. I believe a woman's beauty lies in producing a balance between the body and mind.
Keep that in mind if you want to truly learn about beauty.
I understand. Keeping a balance between the body and mind is important!
That's right. Come see me again if you want to keep learning the secrets of true beauty.
Go get some yin er at the pharmacy. It's a type of Chinese medicine that does wonders for your skin.
You have bags under your eyes. In fact, you're looking rather haggard, dear.
What!? Really!?
Oh, you didn't notice? You really are a bumpkin.
How long have you been an idol?
Umm, about six months.
Six months... Well, I suppose there's a lot you're not used to yet.
Yes, there's so much I'm experiencing for the first time. It's kind of overwhelming.
Says the girl with a smile on her face. I bet you could handle anything that came your way.
This is what I've always wanted, so I'm never going to give up, no matter what.
You got spunk, I'll give you that, but your body is telling a whole other story. Health-wise, you're anything but beautiful right now.
You're young, so a little rest would work wonders. Knowing you, though, I'm sure resting is the last thing you want to do.
That's true. I'd really like to focus on my lessons and work.
I thought you might say that, so let me tell you how to lighten the load a bit.
Go get some yin er at the pharmacy.
It's very popular, but I've instructed the pharmacy to hold some for you.
Um... What was that stuff called again?
That's what's wrong with kids today, always distracted. It's called yin er.
Yin er? That's its Chinese name? What does it do?
It's a type of Chinese medicine that's essential in my skincare regimen. I'll tell you more later, but for now, just go pick it up.
(Er, what was the name of that Chinese medicine Yoko-san wanted me to buy?)
Um, do you have any yi yi ren here?
Huh? Yi yi ren?
(Maybe I didn't say it right.)
Ah, yes, we have plenty of diuretics if you're having trouble relieving yourself.
Oh, yes. Coix seed. It promotes urination, among a variety of other beneficial effects.
I must've gotten the name wrong. I'll be back!
(That was embarrassing. I better go find out what that medicine's called before I try again.)
Um, do you have any yin yang huo here?
Huh? Yin yang huo?
Young lady, I don't think you have any need for this... Or is your boyfriend having problems keeping it up?
Wait, no!
That's definitely not what I want! I must've gotten the name wrong. I'll be back!
Um, do you have any yin er here?
Huh? Yin er?
Yes, Yoko-san contacted you about it and asked me to pick it up.
Oh, yes, of course! We have that ready! Ladies seem to love this. I can hardly keep it on the shelves!
(Whew, I thought I'd gotten the name wrong.)
Sorry to keep you waiting. Here it is.
(Okay, I've got the Chinese medicine, so it's back to Yoko-san's place!)
Interested in another dance battle against me?
Maybe later, okay?
Heh. Well, you know where to find me.
I won't lose to you this time!
You're on! And if you win, your treatment is free! Well, it's time to bust a move!
Whoa! Did I actually win!?
I guess you're just no match for me, Haruka-san! Come on back when you're ready to try again.
No way! Did I actually lose!?
I... I did it!
Impressive. No wonder you've made it to the Princess League finals.
You know about that?
Yep. Been rooted to the TV cheering you on.
Now get ready for the treatment of your life, free of charge, just as promised.
Wait, are you saying you're the stylist!?
Hehe, were you expecting someone else?
Well, what do you think?
That... That felt... amazing!
Yeah? Well, I'm glad you liked it!
I feel so refreshed! And my body... I feel like a huge weight has been lifted off my shoulders!
I don't mean to brag, but I'm known around the world for my work, so...
Wow! Really!?
Yeah, but I also have a partner in Tokyo. We practice hard on each other, and as a result⑬
Oh, sorry, but could we continue this another time? I have to go. Thank you so much!
Ah, right. You're probably a little young to hear all the gory details, hehe.
